title: Vectorial bent functions of the Remark 4 form
summary: Construct theoretical vectorial bent functions built from a bent function and an affine transform as in Article 044's Remark 4.

formal_statement.body: Let $n$ be even, let $g:\mathbb F_2^n\to\mathbb F_2$ be bent, and let $A$ be an affine permutation of $\mathbb F_2^n$. Put $h=g\circ A$ and $F=(g,h):\mathbb F_2^n\to\mathbb F_2^2$. When $g+h$ is bent, $F$ is vectorial bent under the source convention. Construct explicit theoretical families of such $F$ (including the six-variable class exhibited in Remark 4), or prove that no admissible family exists under the stated form.

scope.domain: Vectorial bent functions obtained from affine transforms of bent Boolean functions
assumptions: $n$ is even and bent functions use the source Walsh-transform convention
$A$ is an affine permutation of $\mathbb F_2^n$ and $h=g\circ A$
$F=(g,h)$ is vectorial bent exactly when its nonzero components are bent, in particular $g+h$ is bent
The six-variable instance and equivalence class in Article 044 Remark 4 are included
scope.unresolved_remainder: No later inspected result gives a mathematically specified family in the exact $F=(g,g\circ A)$ shape of Remark 4 or a nonexistence proof. Generalized or extended Maiorana--McFarland vectorial constructions use a different parameterization and do not settle this question.

progress.summary: Article 044 asks for theoretical constructions of vectorial bent functions of the exact shape described in Remark 4.
